issues.existing: ornate footed metal vessel with a hinged lid, resting on the figure's lap
issues.observed: the footed vessel stands on the flat stone seat/ledge in front of her, not on her lap
issues.evidence: The goblet's foot rests on a distinctly lighter grey horizontal stone surface whose front edge runs across the frame; that same stone seat continues to the left under the figure. Her gown drapes down and to the right of the vessel, below and beyond the stone surface it stands on. The vessel is clearly supported by masonry, not by fabric or by her knees.

issues.existing: thin circlet of dark thorny branches on the head
issues.observed: an ornate pointed metal crown/tiara with bright specular glints
issues.evidence: The headpiece is a regular, repeating structure of upward points with several small hard specular highlights along it — the signature of worked metal. It does not show the irregular, tangled branching a thorn circlet would. The existing text's own uncertainty note already concedes it may be a thin metal crown, so the flat assertion of 'thorny branches' is not supported.

issues.existing: narrow spire silhouettes on the far right horizon
issues.observed: one narrow spire is resolvable on the right; a plural count cannot be supported
issues.evidence: Only a single slender pointed silhouette stands clear of the darkness on the right beyond the water. The rest of that zone is undifferentiated black. The existing text's own uncertainty note concedes the number cannot be fixed.

issues.observed: a separate round disc held upright in her other hand beside the vessel's rim; no hinge is visible
issues.evidence: The round lit disc is held on edge by her far hand, clear of and above the cup's mouth, with dark space between the disc and the rim. No hinge, pin or connecting arm can be seen joining the two. Whether the disc is the cup's lid, a mirror or a separate object cannot be determined from the image.
